title: Names and departments from the export
prompt: HR wants a quick list of who works where, straight from its export. The starter saves the export as a file; finish `solve(employees_raw)` so it reads that file as CSV and returns each employee's id, name and department.
rules: Fields are separated by `;` and the first line is a header with the column names. Values in double quotes can contain `;`.
Return `employee_id`, `full_name` and `department`, all text, in that order.
Keep every employee line. A field that's empty, or that a short line doesn't have, is NULL.
hints: `spark.read.csv(path)` assumes commas and no header. Two options change that.
With `header=True`, the columns are named after the first line, so you can select them by name.
No types are needed here: the three columns are text anyway.
starter:
def solve(employees_raw):
    path = "/tmp/hr/export"
    employees_raw.write.mode("overwrite").text(path)
    # Read the file at `path` as CSV and return employee_id, full_name and department.
    return employees_raw
explanation: Two options and a select: `spark.read.csv(path, sep=";", header=True).select("employee_id", "full_name", "department")`. `sep` tells Spark where fields end and `header=True` turns the first line into column names instead of a row. The default `PERMISSIVE` mode keeps a short line and leaves the fields it doesn't have as NULL, and quoted titles that contain `;` stay in one piece, so departments don't shift. A schema with only three columns would be a mistake here: a schema matches fields by position, not by name, so its third column would get the job titles.
